chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Suleiman al-Ja'fari, who said:

I was sick to the extent that my flesh wasted away, so I visited Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: 'Would you be pleased if your flesh were to return to you?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Frequent the bathhouse intermittently, for it will cause your flesh to return. And beware of making it a habit, for habitual bathing causes tuberculosis (consumption).'
ai.seo_question: What is the medical advice of Imam al-Rida regarding bathing and weight loss?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Rida (AS), who prescribed intermittent bathing to restore physical vitality while cautioning against the excesses that lead to *al-Sill* (consumption or wasting disease). It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating spiritual guidance with empirical health practices, emphasizing moderation (*wasatiyyah*) in bodily care as a means to preserve the trust of the body.
